1. SuppressAuditStamps — WakeelDb gained `public IDisposable SuppressAuditStamps()` backed by a nesting counter (`_auditStampSuppressions`) and an idempotent `AuditStampSuppression` scope handle. Inside the scope StampEntry skips the Added/Modified branches entirely, so CreatedAt/UpdatedAt/RowVersion/BaseVersion/OriginDevice are written exactly as the caller set them (the sync-import path, ARCHITECTURE §6); the device-id lookup is skipped too. Outside, the stamps apply as before. Tests: SuppressAuditStamps_OnInsert_KeepsEveryCallerSetAuditColumn, _OnUpdate_KeepsTheIncomingRowVersionAndTimestamp, OutsideTheSuppressionScope_TheAutomaticStampsStillApply, and an async + nested-scope test.

2. Soft delete — StampEntry now has a `case EntityState.Deleted:` that flips the entry to Modified, sets DeletedAt (??= now), bumps UpdatedAt/RowVersion, so a physical delete of an official row is impossible through this context (suppression scope keeps the caller's stamps but still converts). Added `public void SoftDelete<T>(T entity) where T : SyncedEntity` (an Added entity is simply detached — nothing to hide). Tests: Remove+SaveChanges leaves the row (raw SQL COUNT(*) = 1) with deleted_at set, hidden from the filtered query, and writes an 'I' then a 'U' change_log entry; RemoveRange over SaveChangesAsync; SoftDelete helper; SoftDelete on a not-yet-inserted entity.

Converters are constructed with their table/column in the naming-convention pass. Tests: the corrupt value is reported exactly once with the right table/column/text, valid text is never reported, the event is retained in Recent, and an end-to-end test asserts the warning reaches a recording ILogger<WakeelDb> once.
